prompt.context: Our client is Healthy Foods Co., a wholesaler serving a variety of clients with food products. The client is currently profitable.
prompt.question: The client wants help finding revenue growth opportunities from their current business. How can we help Healthy Foods Co. drive their revenue growth?

clarifying_info.a: The client serves various customer categories including independent restaurants, chain restaurants, hospitals, school cafeterias, grocery stores, hotels, and others (see Exhibit 1 when requested).

clarifying_info.q: What do customers care about most?
clarifying_info.a: Customer sensitivities ranked highest to lowest: price, convenient delivery, help with location planning, help with menu, web site development, inventory, help with management optimization.
The client is one of the market leaders and is not losing market share.

clarifying_info.q: Is the client growing or declining?
clarifying_info.a: The client is profitable but wants to identify additional revenue growth opportunities from their existing business.

exhibits.title: Total Market Revenues by Customer Type
exhibits.shows: A breakdown of revenues by customer type, listing: Independent restaurants, Chain restaurants, Hospitals, School cafeterias, Grocery stores, and Other.
exhibits.data: Revenue categories: Independent restaurants (largest), Chain restaurants, Hospitals, School cafeterias, Grocery stores, Other

exhibits.title: Client's Share of Wallet by Customer Size
exhibits.shows: A chart plotting share of wallet (0%–70%) against customer size, with customers labeled A through X (A = largest, X = smallest), and two reference lines indicating whether the client is the primary food product supplier or one of many.
exhibits.data: Y-axis: Share of Wallet 0%–70%; X-axis: Customer Size (A = Largest, X = Smallest); bands: 'Client is Primary food product supplier' vs. 'Client is one of many food product suppliers'

exhibits.title: Wallet Size vs. Share of Wallet for Smaller-Revenue-Generating Customer Categories
exhibits.shows: A scatter plot of wallet size ($M) on the Y-axis vs. share of wallet (%) on the X-axis for the smaller-revenue-generating customer categories: Hospitals, Hotels, School cafeterias, Grocery stores, and Chain restaurants.
exhibits.data: Y-axis: Wallet Size $0–$600M; X-axis: Share of Wallet 0%–60%; data points: Hospitals (large wallet, low share), Hotels (large wallet, low share), School cafeterias (mid wallet, mid share), Grocery stores (mid wallet, mid-high share), Chain restaurants (smaller wallet, higher share)

framework: Identify customer segments and their current revenue contributions (Exhibit 1)
Assess share of wallet by customer segment to determine where growth headroom exists (Exhibit 2)
Prioritize segments by wallet size vs. current share of wallet — large wallet + low share = highest growth potential (Exhibit 3)
Develop targeted strategies to increase share of wallet in the highest-potential segments (hospitals and hotels)
Consider customer sensitivities (price, delivery, menu help) when crafting the go-to-market approach

questions.prompt: Which customer categories generate the most revenue for Healthy Foods Co., and what does this tell you about where to focus?
questions.guidance: The candidate should use Exhibit 1 to note that independent restaurants are the largest revenue contributor by far, with other segments (chain restaurants, hospitals, school cafeterias, grocery stores) each contributing smaller but similar amounts. A strong candidate notes this distribution drives two possible growth levers: grow share in the largest segment, or grow share in the smaller segments.

questions.prompt: Given the revenue breakdown, where does the share of wallet analysis suggest growth potential lies?
questions.guidance: Using Exhibit 2, the candidate should recognize that the largest-revenue customers (e.g., independent restaurants, represented by customers A–C on the chart) already have a high share of wallet — the client is already a primary supplier. This means limited room for growth there. The opportunity lies in the smaller-revenue segments where current share of wallet is lower. The candidate should articulate the insight: high share of wallet in top customers = saturated; low share of wallet in mid/small customers = opportunity.

questions.prompt: Among the smaller-revenue customer segments, how would you prioritize which ones to target for growth?
questions.guidance: The candidate should propose wallet size vs. share of wallet as the prioritization framework: segments with large total wallets but low current share of wallet represent the biggest revenue opportunity. Using Exhibit 3, hospitals and hotels sit in the upper-left quadrant (large wallet, low share) and are therefore the top-priority targets. Chain restaurants have smaller wallets and higher existing share, making them lower priority. School cafeterias and grocery stores sit in the middle.

questions.prompt: How would you recommend Healthy Foods Co. increase its share of wallet with hospitals and hotels specifically?
questions.guidance: The candidate should connect customer sensitivities to the strategy. Hospitals: likely sensitive to reliable delivery, food safety/compliance, inventory management — the client should emphasize convenient delivery, inventory support, and potentially help with menu/nutritional planning. Hotels: likely sensitive to menu variety, delivery reliability, pricing — offer tailored menu help, competitive pricing, and logistics support. The candidate should also note that gaining share from 'one of many suppliers' to 'primary supplier' status requires demonstrating superior value on the top-ranked sensitivities.

brainstorming.prompt: List all options the client could use to increase revenue, and justify each.

categories.name: Increase share of wallet in existing customers
ideas: Offer bundled services to become primary supplier
Improve pricing competitiveness for price-sensitive segments

categories.name: Expand into adjacent customer types
ideas: Enter new verticals such as corporate cafeterias or event catering
Pursue large institutional customers not currently served

categories.name: Increase basket size per transaction
ideas: Upsell premium or specialty food products
Introduce value-added services (menu planning, inventory management)
Offer web/digital tools to increase stickiness

categories.name: Improve retention in existing high-share customers
ideas: Deepen relationships with independent restaurant clients through loyalty programs
Ensure needs of current primary-supplier customers are fully met to defend share

recommendation: The largest near-term revenue growth opportunity lies in hospitals and hotels, which have large total purchasing wallets but a low current share allocated to Healthy Foods Co.

Healthy Foods Co. should develop targeted outreach and service packages for these two segments, emphasizing convenient delivery, inventory support, and menu assistance — the sensitivities most relevant to institutional buyers.
risks: Hospitals and hotels may have established supplier relationships or procurement contracts that are difficult to displace
Institutional clients (hospitals) may have compliance and regulatory requirements (dietary standards, certifications) that require investment to meet
Expanding focus to new segments may dilute service quality for the existing high-share independent restaurant base
next_steps: Conduct customer interviews with hospital and hotel procurement leads to validate sensitivities and identify barriers to switching
Assess internal capability gaps (certifications, delivery infrastructure) required to serve institutional clients
Design a pilot program targeting 3–5 hospitals and 3–5 hotels to test the value proposition and refine the sales approach
